items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: I actually studied with Lee Konitz. And that was on Steve’s suggestion. So to study with the older masters before they go.

ctx.x: Do you think you could have made a living to your satisfaction if you had stayed in Sydney?

I already was actually. I was a big fish in a small pond. I was doing Australian Anado Orchestra, I was doing a lot of very high profile projects. For me it was about learning. I wanted to — at the age of 25, it’s sort of, 25 is when I left and it sort of, I look back on it now like I can’t believe I moved to the other side of the world not knowing a single person, the only thing I had lined up was some lessons with Steve Coleman, that’s who I had private lessons with. And then four years later I also got another…
In applying for the grant that made that possible I’m guessing you had to verbalize or write on paper what was your intent, what is it that you were so intent on learning?
